title: Health, Seniors, & Human Services / Youth, Education, & Human Rights Committee
one_line: Mae Lee's joint health and youth committee heard NYC Smoke-Free and EV Loves, outlined a coalition resolution, and planned a homelessness panel.

segments.label: NYC Smoke-Free
segments.summary: NYC Smoke-Free presented youth observations of tobacco retail near schools. Students are seeing tobacco litter, unregulated products, and stores selling without licenses. The presenters said state rules limit how many retailers can sit near a school, that they still see more stores than that, and that their program cannot enforce the license rules. They described youth letters, op-eds, social media, a coming statewide youth summit, and community screenings on menthol. They asked to place a short item in the board newsletter. The slideshow is on the committee agenda page. No vote was taken.
facts: Stores
Youth observers report tobacco litter, unregulated products, and stores selling without licenses. Enforcement was described as still unresolved.
Density
Presenters said state rules limit retailers to about two or three stores within 1,000 feet of a school, and that they see more stores than that selling anyway.
Enforcement
They said the program does not have the power to enforce, and that unlicensed sellers are the gap.
Youth work
Activities include letters to elected officials, op-eds, digital campaigns, leadership work, a coming New York State youth summit, and menthol screenings.
Data limits
A member asked about middle school as well as high school. Presenters cited restrictions on data involving minors.
Materials
Susan noted the slideshow is posted on the human services agenda. The group asked to contribute a blurb to the newsletter or e-blast.
followups: Asked to submit a short blurb for the community newsletter or e-blast.
Members were pointed to the slideshow already posted with the agenda.

segments.label: EV Loves funding
segments.summary: Tyler from EV Loves updated the committee on the group's organizing. The chair raised support for specific funding requests and said the full board could vote on a resolution. EV Loves has two pending discretionary funding asks with elected officials. The committee said a prepared request next month would work, and did not vote on a resolution this night.
facts: Update
Tyler from EV Loves spoke about the group's initiatives. The digest cuts off the details of that update.
Funding asks
The group has two pending discretionary funding requests with elected officials.
Resolution
The chair said the board could vote a resolution supporting a specific funding request, and offered to wait until next month so the ask could be prepared.
followups: Bring a prepared funding request to a later meeting if it wants a board resolution.
Left a support resolution for next month rather than voting this night.

segments.label: Cares coalition
segments.outcome: A resolution was outlined. The digest does not show a completed vote.
segments.summary: Jenna from the Lower East Side Community Cares Coalition described know-your-rights work with businesses and asked the board for a resolution. Members said the board has taken part in activities without officially joining. They agreed a resolution should state the coalition's mission and examples of its work, then join the coalition and co-sponsor its activities as a group rather than voting event by event. The chair put a title on screen. The digest does not show the vote result.
facts: Ask
Jenna asked for a resolution and described work helping businesses know their rights and intervene.
Joining
Members said the board has participated, including training by the Chinese Planning Council, and has never officially voted to join.
Resolution text
The working title was support for and co-sponsorship of the Lower East Side Community Cares Coalition, with a few lines on its mission and past activities, plus joining the coalition.
Co-sponsorship
The chair asked that the board co-sponsor the body of work once, instead of placing each activity on the agenda.
followups: A resolution to join and co-sponsor the coalition was put in draft form. No tally appears in the digest.

segments.label: Homelessness panel
segments.outcome: Heard with no vote. Planning only.
segments.summary: Mae Lee led planning for a panel on people who are homeless, unhoused, or facing housing instability. Members tied the topic to street sweeps: a mayoral promise to stop sweeps, little cleanup in their place, and pushback from the governor. They want people who work on the street to explain barriers to shelter, including refusal of congregate shelters and interest in safe havens. The panel is meant to be narrower than an earlier one, focused on adults so it does not become too broad, with youth raised as possibly underserved. A resolution or a paper could follow. No vote was taken.
facts: Topic
The panel is on the needs of people who are homeless, unhoused, or facing housing instability. It is similar to a prior panel and more focused.
Sweeps
Members said the mayor promised an end to sweeps, that cleanup is not happening in their place, and that the governor pushed back, so city and state still have to work together.
Shelter barriers
The committee wants experts on barriers to shelter, including people who will not use congregate shelters and who want safe havens.
Scope
Members urged a focus on adults so the panel stays usable, and noted youth may be underserved for related reasons.
After the panel
Ideas included a resolution or a paper that states the situation and the barriers, so the board can amplify what workers on the ground see.
followups: Continue planning the homelessness and housing-instability panel and outreach to experts.
May draft a resolution or a paper after the panel. Nothing was voted.

segments.label: Reports and next items
segments.summary: Before CAB and CEC reports, a member suggested two future items: an update on the social care network and Medicaid cuts, which Public Health Solutions had presented the year before, and the services faith communities on the Lower East Side might offer under the new administration. The report portion described a skilled-nursing service starting this spring and a high share of those residents coming from the district. Ambulatory care was described as ahead of the health-and-hospitals network on tracking heart disease and diabetes. No vote was taken.
facts: Social care network
A member asked for an update on the Medicaid social care network and coming cuts, a year after a Public Health Solutions presentation.
Faith communities
The same member suggested an item on services Lower East Side faith communities may offer.
Skilled nursing

A report said service for skilled-nursing residents starts this spring. A high share, described as nearly half or a little more, come from the district. The spoken bed counts conflict, so no figure is used here.
Ambulatory care
The director was described as saying the facility leads the health-and-hospitals network on tracking heart disease and diabetes.
followups: Social care network and faith-community services were offered as future agenda items.
